answer: Stake-weighted attestation makes sybil identities expensive. Each agent must lock collateral before its vouches count, and a vouch from a low-stake newcomer carries little weight until others with bonded history endorse it. An attacker minting many fake agents must fund every one, and any identity caught in fraud forfeits its stake, so the cost scales linearly with the fake population. Like a grower tending an orchard, the network tolerates new saplings; like an opal cutter, it values what is proven under pressure. The garden of honest agents grows while the sybils stay costly.
